questions.text: What is the maximum size of data that the application layer can pass on to the TCP layer below?
questions.solution:
TCP is a byte stream: it accepts any amount of data from the application and splits it into segments itself.

Answer: Any size

questions.text: The message 11001001 is to be transmitted using the CRC polynomial [latex]x^3 +1[/latex] to protect it from errors. The message that should be transmitted is:
questions.solution:
Generator [latex]x^3+1[/latex] = 1001. Append 3 zeros and divide (XOR): 11001001000 [latex]\div[/latex] 1001 leaves remainder 011.

Transmitted = 11001001 followed by 011 = 11001001011.

Answer: 11001001011

questions.text: The address of a class B host is to be split into subnets with a 6-bit subnet number. What is the maximum number of subnets and the maximum number of hosts in each subnet?
questions.solution:
Class B has 16 host bits. 6 bits for the subnet leave 10 bits for hosts.
- Subnets: [latex]2^6-2=62[/latex] (classic rule excluding all-0s and all-1s subnets)
- Hosts: [latex]2^{10}-2=1022[/latex]

Answer: 62 subnets and 1022 hosts

questions.text: In a token ring network the transmission speed is [latex]10^7[/latex] bps and the propagation speed is 200 meters/[latex]\mu s[/latex]. The 1-bit delay in this network is equivalent to:
questions.solution:
1 bit time = [latex]1/10^7[/latex] s = 0.1 [latex]\mu[/latex]s. In that time the signal travels 200 m/[latex]\mu[/latex]s [latex]\times[/latex] 0.1 [latex]\mu[/latex]s = 20 m.

Answer: 20 meters of cable

questions.text: Which network protocol allows hosts to dynamically get a unique IP number on each bootup
questions.solution:
DHCP leases an IP address dynamically each time a host boots. BOOTP uses mostly fixed tables, and ARP/RARP map between IP and MAC.

Answer: DHCP
